rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests the foundational multimodal approach (combining RNA and image data) with simple concatenation fusion, which is a critical design choice. It clarifies whether multimodal modeling improves performance compared to single-modality baselines, providing insight into the most impactful design decision. This is the best use of the first experiment as it directly addresses the core hypothesis of the study.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000+resnet50, concat fusion) achieves 0.526 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' improves performance, a critical design choice in multimodal models. It directly addresses uncertainty about fusion strategies while building on the existing multimodal setup, balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows that fusion methods (concat vs weighted) have minimal impact on accuracy (0.5266 vs 0.5232). The next experiment should test aggregation methods (avgpool) in a multiprofile setting, which is unexplored. This clarifies whether aggregation strategies significantly affect performance in more complex scenarios, balancing exploration of key design choices (aggregation) with the multimodal framework.

The existing evidence shows that config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.6186). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' (config_019) could further improve performance, directly building on the strong foundation of config_018. It clarifies the importance of fusion strategy while exploiting the proven effectiveness of the other design choices.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, weighted fusion, and avgpool aggregation (config_019) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.639). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with the more powerful imagenet_vit_l image encoder and switching to transformer aggregation (which may capture complex interactions) while retaining weighted fusion. This clarifies whether upgrading the image encoder and aggregation method can further improve performance, building on the success of weighted fusion in multiprofile settings.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.638999). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated encoder) in this high-performing setup improves performance, clarifying the impact of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the current top-performing architecture with exploration of a key design decision.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and avgpool aggregation (e.g., config_031) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether the RNA-only variant with the same encoder and aggregation (config_005) can match or exceed this performance, clarifying the value of multimodal integration. It directly addresses whether the RNA encoder's quality (scvi_n200) alone is sufficient to achieve high accuracy, which is critical for understanding design tradeoffs under limited budget.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests whether upgrading the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced model) further improves performance, clarifying the impact of image encoder choice on multimodal multiprofile models.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion (config_037) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation (config_039) could further improve performance. It clarifies the impact of aggregation methods on multimodal multiprofile models, a critical design choice with potential for significant gains.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (config_039: 0.725). This experiment tests whether switching to the more advanced scgpt RNA encoder and transformer aggregation (instead of avgpool) could further improve performance, clarifying the impact of these key design choices. It balances exploitation (building on prior success) and exploration (testing new encoder/aggregation combinations).
